requiredBoundaries.evidence: Migration 034 implements locked logical ownership, unique player/campaign and character claims, release, claimed-player save and no direct runtime table privileges. The real PostgreSQL 17 harness installed 026-034, ran as hollowgate_api_runtime and produced exactly one committed claim plus one assignment per claim, an atomic release that deleted both rows, and a membership trigger that removed claim and assignment in the same transaction.

Real Chromium GM context merged owner-scoped claims with assignments from PostgreSQL, required exact agreement, kept physical GM ownership and rendered the claimed card under the verified player row with the locked-assignment notice; after release the grouping disappeared while the edited name persisted. No stale claim grouping survived a full GM re-entry.

Real Chromium player claimed through the shipping UI, opened the original detail and saved a renamed sheet: PUT returned 200 and PostgreSQL stored the new name. save_claimed_character_sheet authorizes the current claim and membership on every write; after membership revocation the same stale PUT returned 404 and the database kept the previous name.

Real Chromium claimant uploaded a PNG portrait (PUT 200) against PostgreSQL. After release the claimant PUT returned 404 while the physical GM PUT returned 200. After a later reclaim plus membership revocation the claimant PUT returned 404 again, proving authorization follows the live claim and membership.

With the real claim active, the player-scoped asset list returned the referenced portrait-frame asset and its content endpoint returned 200 through PostgreSQL. Release and membership revocation each emptied the player asset list and returned 404 for the same referenced content; the claimed UI never wrote shared assets.

Real PostgreSQL set_campaign_membership(active=false) deleted the claim and assignment atomically. The open Chromium detail then received 404 on sheet save and portrait upload, the player asset list became empty, /vtt/player-campaigns stopped listing the campaign and a full reload showed no campaign entry.

Real HTTP handlers behind the shipping Vite proxy derived identity from the __Host-hg_session cookie. Bootstrap reported characterClaims and playerCharacters reads enabled; a foreign Origin claim returned 403, an empty invalid body returned 400, and all claim, release, save, portrait and asset responses passed exact status/shape assertions.

browser-character-claim-real-db.mjs drives the shipping CampaignHome in Chromium against real HTTP and PostgreSQL: claim from Precompilati, Personaggi listing, original claimed detail editing, release to GM, empty-state message, re-entry and both GM and player views were exercised without page errors. This supersedes the earlier stateful HTTP fixture proof.

browser-character-claim-real-db.mjs runs three real Chromium contexts against disposable PostgreSQL. An admin SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the character row held both browser claims in pg_stat_activity (two lock waiters) before COMMIT; the two responses were exactly one 200 and one 409, PostgreSQL kept the single winning claim/assignment and the losing UI displayed the authoritative 'Personaggio non più disponibile' failure. Release, reclaim, membership revocation and stale-write denial were then re-proven in the same session.
